pass_b_english: The law will emanate from Zion and the word of the Lord will be proclaimed from Jerusalem, and it will announce to us His way, and we will walk in it (Isaiah 2:3).

As the memory of the prophecy over them has come, the prophet indicates the time during which the power of the devil will not fall on any part of the earth or in one place and city, but rather this disease will be taken from all under heaven, and the tyranny of the unclean demons will be broken, with the worship of idols and the wicked construction having been removed from everywhere.

The vision has ended for him, and the end of the prophecy that has already arrived was, because they will be ashamed of their idols, which they wanted, and they were ashamed of their gardens, which they desired.

In the way that the Israelites were ashamed of their idols, which they had desired, they will also be ashamed of their gardens, which they had desired, and this shame is a continuous theme that we have discussed.

In the last days, that is, in the last times of the present age, the only-begotten Word of God has shone, having become from a woman, and He has presented to Himself the intelligible Judah, that is, Jerusalem, that is, the virgin Church, pure and unblemished, without stain or wrinkle, as it is written: holy and unblemished (Ephesians 5:27).
The prophet says about the Church that in the last days, the mountain of the Lord will be manifest, and the house of God of Jacob will be established on the tops of the mountains.
To us, Zion, which is in Judea, is said to be situated on a mountain and built, but one would think of the Church, not sensibly, but spiritually, as being likened to a mountain.

The Church is truly high and conspicuous, and well-known to all, for it is elevated above earthly things and, as far as possible, contemplates God's glory with the eyes of the mind, boasting of lofty doctrines about Him.

In contrast, the Greek sophists, who deify creation and pay homage to the elements of the world, demonstrate their lowly mind and earthly speculations, and, claiming to be wise, they became fools, as it is written (Romans 1:22).

The Church surpasses all visible and invisible creation, and reaches the nature that is beyond all things, for it is filled with divine light, and, knowing itself and the Creator and Artisan of all things, it alone receives the power that is over all things.
And with this glory He will crown.
